A real zero of \(f(x)\) corresponds to an \(x\)-intercept of its graph.

On the interval \([-6,6]\), the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at
\[
x=-3,\ -1,\ 1,\ 3.
\]
The curve does not touch or cross the \(x\)-axis anywhere else in this interval, and the endpoints \(x=-6,6\) are not zeros.

Therefore, the number of distinct real zeros is
\[
\boxed{4}
\]
